name: enemies-r10
note: The Ogre redrawn for an arm rig and a club (owner, 2026-11-13: 'give the Ogre a club and have him swing it'; the prototype for held equipment). Same design; leaner round the middle so the belly no longer hides the arm; both arms hang free of the body with background between arm and torso (the art rule of docs/arm-rig-plan.md); a club in the hand on the viewer's right (the facing arm: the art faces right), hanging down in line with the forearm and clear of the leg, so arm and club cut as one piece. This replaces the rule that enemies hold nothing, for this enemy.

ogre.prompt: RENDERING REFERENCE: the attached COW on magenta is one of this game's animals: match its rendering (soft painterly, flat colour with gentle shading, soft thick outlines, no texture, no background). STYLE REFERENCE, the most important image: the attached farm man on magenta is an APPROVED character of this game. The new creature must look drawn by the same hand on the same day, for the same storybook: the same chunky doll proportion (a big head, large expressive eyes, a short thick body, small feet), the same soft rendering; never realistic, never anatomical, never gory. THIS IS AN ENEMY the player fights: menacing in a storybook way (a scowl, bared teeth, a glare), but still charming and readable, something a child would call a monster and not be frightened by; no blood, no wounds. VIEW, the rule for every enemy (unlike this game's farm animals, which are drawn side-on): FRONT-FACING, like the player characters: upright and facing the viewer, the body square-ish to the viewer with a FAINT three-quarter turn, the head and the eyes turned a little toward the viewer's RIGHT, standing on ONE flat ground line, left and right sides roughly symmetrical, nothing trailing far outside the body's silhouette. SIBLINGS: the attached ZOMBIE and the attached brown BEAR are approved enemies of this game: the ogre must look painted by the same hand: the same simple rounded shapes, clean flat-ish colour with gentle soft shading, soft thick outlines, a slightly big head and a clear readable face. DESIGN REFERENCE: the attached OGRE is the approved drawing of this enemy. Keep its design, face, colours and rendering EXACTLY: the bald head with a rough strip of dark hair behind, the pointed ears, the heavy brow, the grim scowl with an underbite and two short blunt tusks, the slightly green olive skin, the bare chest, the dark leather wrappings on both forearms, the ragged dark brown kilt under a wide belt with an iron ring buckle, the wrapped shins, the huge bare feet. Redraw him with THREE changes, because his arm will be animated. CHANGE 1, HE HAS LOST WEIGHT ROUND THE MIDDLE: a broad chest and thick round shoulders over a firm, much smaller belly that does not bulge out past the chest; the torso tapers from the shoulders to a waist clearly NARROWER than the shoulders. He is still a huge, heavy, thick-limbed brute, only no longer pot-bellied. CHANGE 2, THE ARMS HANG FREE OF THE BODY, as the attached bear's forelegs do: both arms hang down at his sides in a relaxed, natural stance, a little away from the body, elbows soft, hands at hip level; NOT a stiff T-pose and not spread wide, but with a clear strip of the magenta background showing between each WHOLE arm and the torso, the hip and the kilt, from the armpit all the way down to the hand. No part of either arm overlaps the chest, the belly, the kilt or the legs, and neither arm is tucked behind the body. Both arms are the same full thickness with big round shoulders. CHANGE 3, A CLUB: in the hand on the viewer's RIGHT he grips a heavy wooden CLUB by its handle in a closed fist. The club is a thick knotted tree limb: narrow at the grip, swelling to a fat rounded head with three short blunt iron studs, plain dark brown wood. It hangs straight DOWN from his fist, in line with his forearm, its heavy head a little above the ground beside his foot, about as long as his forearm and hand together. The WHOLE club lies outside his leg and kilt with magenta background between the club and the leg; it overlaps nothing and nothing overlaps it. The hand on the viewer's LEFT is empty and open. He stands on ONE flat ground line, feet planted a little apart. Keep it at the game's scale: it is seen about 60 pixels wide on the board, so big plain shapes, a strong silhouette, flat areas of colour, no fine detail, no small accessories. COLOUR: never pink, never magenta, never purple anywhere on it. The LAST attached image is a layout guide: a pure magenta (#FF00FF) field with a thin grid, a 1 x 1 box outlined in the middle (one board tile) and a dashed half-height box directly above it (the headroom); the reference character stands in that box with its head in the headroom. ONE FIGURE ONLY, nothing else in the picture: no building, no props on the ground, no scene. Draw him standing on the box's bottom edge and bigger than the reference character: about one and a half times as tall, his feet on the box's bottom edge, his head near the top of the headroom; with the arms and the club he may be wider than the box. A soft contact shadow directly under it; leave every other pixel pure solid magenta: no grass, no ground, no frame, no text.
